turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi Maria, good to see you again. How have things been since your last visit in October?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Honestly, it's been a rough month. The pain in my lower back has been worse, and it's going down my left leg more.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm sorry to hear that. On a scale of 0 to 10, where has your pain been most days?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Most days it's about a 6. On bad days it's an 8. It's a sharp, stabbing pain, not just an ache.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How many bad days would you say you've had this past month?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Maybe eight or nine. Two of those days I had to leave work early.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're at the school district office, right? Is it the sitting?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, I'm at a desk all day doing payroll. After about an hour of sitting, it starts burning down my leg.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And how are you sleeping?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not good. I wake up three or four times a night because of the pain. I'm tired all the time.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Something a lot of my patients find helpful is a heating pad for 15 to 20 minutes and some gentle stretching before bed. Have you tried that?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I haven't. I can try it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything new since last time? Any numbness or tingling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Actually, yes. For about two weeks my left foot has been tingling, mostly in the toes. It comes and goes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you for telling me. Any weakness, trouble walking, or problems with your bladder or bowels?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that. Just the tingling.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good. Let's go over your medicines. You're taking gabapentin 300 milligrams three times a day?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. Morning, afternoon, and bedtime.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And meloxicam 15 milligrams once a day?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, with breakfast. And sometimes Tylenol in the evening, maybe two or three times a week.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any side effects? Dizziness, upset stomach?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I get a little dizzy in the morning from the gabapentin, but it goes away after about an hour.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How is physical therapy going?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I go once a week, with Kevin at Riverside PT. It's been six weeks… maybe seven. The core exercises help. I do them at home three days a week.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's great, keep that up. Let me check your back and legs. When I raise your left leg like this, does that bring on the pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, that's it. It shoots down the back of my leg.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Your reflexes and strength look normal, which is good. Pain with the leg raise on the left points to an irritated nerve in your lower back. Here's my plan. First, I'd like to raise your bedtime gabapentin to 600 milligrams. Keep taking 300 in the morning and afternoon. That may help the nerve pain and your sleep.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Will that make me more dizzy?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It might a little at first, which is why we're adding it at bedtime. If the dizziness gets worse or you feel unsteady, call us. Second, because of the new tingling, I'm referring you to Dr. Patel at the Spine Center for an evaluation. They may want an MRI.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Should I keep going to PT?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes, keep PT once a week and your home exercises. Let's see you back in six weeks, on January 5th. Call sooner if the tingling spreads or you notice any weakness.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: January 5th. Okay, thank you, Dr. Lee.
